rv.q: This spot-on production from the RSC, transferring from Stratford, reminds us once more, in this centenary year of Miller's birth, of Salesman's greatness.
In Miller's centenary year, this is a fine birthday present: his greatest and trickiest play, done just right.
You’re unlikely to see a better production of it than this one.
It's a deeply admirable production, from the central performance of Antony Sher as Willy Loman – a loose companion to Sher's Lear coming next year – to the vast vertical set by Stephen Brimson Lewis.
This is a fine production of a painful play which may well succeed in attracting throngs of Americans.

cn.t: The RSC's traditional revival earns strong praise for Antony Sher's central performance and its faithful approach to Miller's classic, though it lacks the avant-garde excitement of recent West End productions.
